As more driverless cars are introduced they can network together to help plan ahead, and avoid accidents. This could lead to improved traffic flow and less accidents. Additionally, removing the possibility of human error will help avoid accidents with the implementation of machine systems such as auto breaking, lane keeping, sonar and lidar, which can prevent accidents as they detect threats that humans may not have seen. One issue with driverless cars is if the car meets a zero-sum problem, eg you are in a situation where a fatal accident is unavoidable - does the car prioritize the safety of the driver if it will cause a fatality to someone else?
candidate_text: Honestly, as a person, I'm still on the fence about this - I can see arguments going both ways. On one hand, driverless cars could potentially reduce accidents caused by human error, like distracted driving or speeding, which are a huge problem on our roads. But on the other hand, I worry about the technology failing or not being able to react to unexpected situations, which could also lead to accidents. Not to mention, there are so many variables at play, like how these cars will interact with human-driven vehicles and pedestrians. I think it's going to take a lot of testing and data to really understand the impact, and even then, it's hard to predict how it will all play out.
